answer: Sybil resistance here is stake-and-slash: each agent identity must lock a bond before its vote counts. A bot army therefore pays one full bond per fake node, so cost grows linearly with the number of Sybils. If a challenger proves two nodes share one controller, both bonds are slashed and the challenger takes a bounty. A knoll of duplicate accounts gains no extra weight, hollow clones collapse into a single vote, and any node caught equivocating falls over the ledge, losing its stake. The attacker ends up funding the very bounty that exposes them.
